A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InftyThink work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, with retained material identifiable across moves and renumbering.

before.justification: v4 reports original fine-tuning and evaluation results, including accuracy, token counts, latency, ablations and coding benchmark results.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results and adds prompt-only comparisons, a summarization-context ablation, additional stability results and reasoning examples.

M1.justification: The iterative reasoning procedure, summary-conditioned continuation, stopping mechanism and training-data reconstruction remain unchanged. Cumulative-history summarization was already specified in v4; v5 clarifies and tests that existing design.

E1.justification: Both versions use OpenR1-Math and OpenThoughts, evaluating the same mathematics, science and coding benchmarks, including HumanEval/MBPP and their Plus variants. The new ablations and cases use retained tasks rather than adding coverage.

E2.justification: v5 Section 4.4 adds a prompt-only iterative comparator using R1-distill-Qwen-1.5B, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct or Llama3.3-70B-Instruct as summarizers. These configurations are newly compared against trained InftyThink in Table 3. Existing vanilla, RoPE and literature comparison methods remain.

E3.justification: v5 introduces focused protocols for prompt-only reasoning at eta=4k, local versus cumulative summary construction, and FLOPs-based evaluation excluding initial prompt costs. It also changes the reported distilled-model size from 7B to 1.5B in Section 3.1 and corresponding tables while retaining scores; this does not establish reruns. Existing main training and decoding budgets remain.

E4.justification: New controls examine whether iterative reasoning requires training (Section 4.4) and whether summaries must preserve global history (Appendix I). Appendix R.2 adds FLOPs-versus-accuracy analysis, and Appendix U adds actual reasoning cases. These substantially extend investigation of the method's mechanisms and efficiency beyond v4's retained ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions report three training runs and evaluation averages over 16 samples at temperature 0.7 and top_p 0.95. v5 adds 7B result rows using the existing reporting practice, without introducing confidence intervals, significance tests or a changed run-count policy.

E6.justification: Existing headline numerical values are retained, but substantial results are added. For Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B, new Table 7 reports local-summary accuracies of 77.18/19.48/29.78 versus retained global-summary values of 79.57/26.04/35.89 on MATH500/AIME24/GPQA_diamond. Other additions include prompt-only scores, context-cap accuracies, 7B repeated-run results, FLOPs curves and individual reasoning outputs.

T1.justification: Appendix R.2 adds an approximate KV-cache FLOPs model separating linear projection, FFN and output-head costs from quadratic attention costs, then summing costs across iterations. Existing method equations and squared-token reasoning remain; the added TOK formulas clarify an existing metric.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about iterative summarization, extended reasoning depth, computational efficiency, accuracy improvements and avoiding architectural modifications. The new analyses support these claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v5 attributes prompt-only shortcomings to training mismatch and summarization overhead, and local-summary losses to forgotten intermediate conclusions. Appendix R.2 adds an interpretation of efficiency gains depending on model size, sequence length and FFN versus attention costs. The existing limitations discussion is retained.

D1.justification: v5 clarifies generated-token accounting and iteration-curve aggregation, and supplies architectural parameters for its FLOPs calculations. Direct code and dataset links disappear from the front page; a new reproducibility statement points to supplementary implementation scripts and promises data release, while retaining the project page. Actual resource withdrawal is not established.

R1.justification: v5 adds the HumanEval and MBPP references and cites InftyThink+ in the reinforcement-learning future direction. The related-work taxonomy and positioning otherwise remain stable. Numerous venue and year updates concern already cited works.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains closely matched, with localized clarification and restructuring of the cost and metric appendices. v5 adds Section 4.4 and publication declarations, and updates the conference header and correspondence details. The overall narrative is retained.

P2.justification: Visual exposition expands substantially through a new six-panel FLOPs figure, ablation and architecture tables, and boxed traces displaying reasoning iterations and summaries. Context-hit and stability tables expand. Existing plots are retained, with the two eta-analysis figures consolidated onto one page and selected captions clarified.

improvement.justification: The prompt-only and global-summary controls address gaps in v4's validation, while additional stability evidence, FLOPs analysis and token accounting improve assessment of the existing method. These are incremental gains over an already extensive evaluation. The cost model still omits initial prompt costs, and direct code/data access becomes less explicit.
